name: codex
description: OpenAI Codex CLI in non-interactive mode (`codex exec`). Uses Codex's own sandbox levels as the policy axis, which is a cleaner operationalisation than a tool allow-list: the restriction is enforced by the sandbox, not by asking the model to abstain.
verificationNote: Verified against a live install (codex-cli 0.147.0, authenticated via ChatGPT). `codex exec --ignore-user-config --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check "<prompt>"` was run and returned the answer as plain stdout ('This project uses the MIT License.'), so output.type is "text" -- no JSON or JSONL parsing is involved. --ignore-user-config is set so the run does not inherit whatever MCP servers and settings the operator has in ~/.codex/config.toml, giving a reproducible baseline; auth still resolves via CODEX_HOME, so this does not require re-login. NOT captured: cost and token counts. Codex reports usage only on its --json event stream, and adding a JSONL parser purely to read a token count was judged not worth the per-agent parsing burden it reintroduces, so cost shows n/a for this agent.
